title: Event loop & microtasks
description: Sync runs first. Microtasks (Promise.then) drain COMPLETELY before the next macrotask (setTimeout). That is why a Promise.then logs before a setTimeout(_, 0).

notes: Sync code always runs first. Microtasks (Promise.then, queueMicrotask) drain before the next macrotask.
A .then enqueued inside another .then waits for the rest of the current microtask level to drain.
setTimeout(fn, 0) is NOT zero delay — it schedules a macrotask, so any pending Promise.then runs first.

questions.q: In `console.log("A"); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("B")); console.log("C");`, what prints?
A Promise.then callback is which kind of task?
Between two sync statements, can a setTimeout(_, 0) callback fire?
options: No — sync code runs to completion before any task fires
Yes, but only after the next microtask drain interleaves
Yes, if `await` yields the thread between the two statements

questions.q: Why does Promise.then beat setTimeout(_, 0) to the punch?
options: Promises have higher priority by spec
Microtask queue drains fully before the next macrotask runs
Both — priority and the 4 ms floor

exercises.prompt: Predict the order: write the three logs so the output matches A, C, B.
Fill the chain so the output is 4, 1, 3, 2.

blanks.hint: logs after 1 in the same microtask level

L3.prompt: Log "start", schedule chain `.then(log "micro1").then(log "micro2")`, then log "end". Expect: start, end, micro1, micro2.
hints: Microtask queue drains: micro1 → which queues micro2 → micro2 runs.
